topic.title: Toolbar and Contextual Menu Actions of the Compare Directories Tool

body.p: The toolbar of the Compare Directories tool provides actions for working with the compared directory structure. Some toolbar actions are also available from the contextual menu.

Opens the Directory Comparison preferences pageOpens a Directory Comparison preferences page where you can configure various options.
Displays a less cluttered file structure by hiding identical files.

Saves the current directory comparison results as an XML report file. The report captures the full comparison tree (matching file pairs and their diff status), file comparison options, include/exclude filter patterns, and the comparison mode. You can later reload the saved report in the Compare Directories tool using the Load XML Report action (available from the File menu), without repeating the comparison.
Generates an HTML file that contains detailed information about the comparison result.

dd.p: You can filter differences using the following combo boxes: Include files, Include folders, Exclude files, and Exclude folders. Each combo box includes predefined values and can be edited to add custom values. All filters accept multiple comma-separated values and the * and ? wildcards. Each filter also includes a drop-down menu that lists the 15 most recently applied filters.

For example, to filter out all JPEG and GIF image files, set the Exclude files filter box to *.jpeg, *.png. To include only a specific subfolder in the comparison (e.g. topics/very-recent), set the Include folders filter to topi*/ve*rece* or topi*\ve*rece*, choosing the appropriate file separator for your operating system.

p.note: Instead of editing a filter combo box directly, press Ctrl+Shift+E (Meta+Shift+E on macOS) while the text field has focus to open a specialized filter editor dialog box. You can edit any previously used filter stored in the history or create a new filter. You can also select multiple previous filters and combine them as is to create a new composite filter, or edit the result of the multiple selection as needed. To remove previous filters from the history, select them and press Delete (Fn+Backspace on macOS).
